title: On being told to relax
summary_es: Monólogo humorístico: un hombre incapaz de relajarse cuenta la semana que pasó, a su pesar, en un retiro de bienestar.
prediction_prompt: British humour often works by understatement: saying less than you mean. Listen for what the speaker does not say outright.

segments.speaker: martin
segments.text: My doctor says I need to relax, which is exactly the sort of thing that stops me relaxing.

segments.speaker: martin
segments.text: It's like being told not to think about your tongue. Now it's all you've got.

segments.speaker: martin
segments.text: So my wife booked us a week at what the brochure called a wellness retreat.

segments.speaker: martin
segments.text: I've noticed that anything calling itself a retreat is, strategically speaking, an admission of defeat.

segments.speaker: martin
segments.text: We were greeted by a man named Sky, who had clearly never been rained on in his life.

segments.speaker: martin
segments.text: He asked whether I'd set an intention for the week.

segments.speaker: martin
segments.text: I said my intention was to leave on Saturday, and he wrote that down.

segments.speaker: martin
segments.text: The first morning there was a silent breakfast, which I assumed was a marital dispute in progress.

segments.speaker: martin
segments.text: Forty adults, chewing mindfully. I have never been so aware of other people's toast.

segments.speaker: martin
segments.text: Then came yoga. I'm told the body keeps the score. Mine keeps receipts, and it wanted a refund.

segments.speaker: martin
segments.text: The instructor said to breathe into my hips, which is anatomically ambitious.

segments.speaker: martin
segments.text: She said, let your thoughts drift past like clouds. Mine don't drift. Mine circle, like a traffic helicopter.

segments.speaker: martin
segments.text: By Wednesday I'd found the only other sceptic, a retired judge hiding in the car park.

segments.speaker: martin
segments.text: We'd meet behind the bins, the two of us, like teenagers, sharing a contraband packet of crisps.

segments.speaker: martin
segments.text: He told me he'd sentenced people to less than this.

segments.speaker: martin
segments.text: On Thursday they took our phones away for something called a digital sunset.

segments.speaker: martin
segments.text: I don't mind admitting I grieved. I went through all five stages before lunch.

segments.speaker: martin
segments.text: And then, annoyingly, something happened. I sat on a bench with nothing to check.

segments.speaker: martin
segments.text: And after about an hour of twitching, I noticed a tree. A fairly ordinary tree.

segments.speaker: martin
segments.text: I must have looked at it for twenty minutes. I couldn't tell you why.

segments.speaker: martin
segments.text: It wasn't doing anything. I think that was rather the point.

segments.speaker: martin
segments.text: I mentioned this to Sky, and he nodded as if he'd arranged the tree personally.

segments.speaker: martin
segments.text: I'm not saying I'm cured. I checked my email in the taxi, with the hunger of a released prisoner.

segments.speaker: martin
segments.text: But I've since bought a bench. It's in the garden. I've sat on it twice.

segments.speaker: martin
segments.text: My wife says that's progress. My doctor says it's a start.

segments.speaker: martin
segments.text: And the judge says he's coming round on Sunday, with crisps.

connected_speech.explanation_es: *you've* queda reducido a /juːv/ entre dos palabras fuertes: si se pierde la /v/, parece «all you got».
Las dos *t* finales no explotan: se cortan en la garganta (oclusión glotal), muy típico del inglés británico actual.
La *'d* de *I'd* (= I had) apenas se oye y la *d* de *found* desaparece delante de *the*.
*must have* suena «mástav», y *looked at it* se enlaza en una sola unidad.
Consonante + vocal encadenadas: *sat on it* suena como una sola palabra.

options.text: Recommending a wellness centre to people who suffer from stress
Complaining to a doctor about his treatment
Telling a comic story about a holiday he resisted
Explaining the health benefits of yoga

tasks.rationale_es: Es un monólogo de humor: cuenta, con ironía constante, la semana en un retiro al que fue arrastrado.

tasks.prompt: How has his attitude changed by the end?

options.text: He grudgingly admits it had some effect
He has become an enthusiastic believer in everything the retreat teaches
He is angrier than before
He regrets ever having gone

tasks.rationale_es: *annoyingly, something happened*: muy a su pesar, algo funcionó. No está «curado», pero se ha comprado un banco.

tasks.prompt: What is the joke in "anything calling itself a retreat is an admission of defeat"?

options.text: He thinks the brochure was written by soldiers
He plays on the military sense of the word
He believes that wellness centres always lose money in the end
He has mixed up two similar-sounding words

tasks.rationale_es: *Retreat* es un retiro de descanso, pero también la retirada de un ejército: *strategically speaking* delata el doble sentido.

tasks.prompt: What does he suggest by saying Sky "had clearly never been rained on in his life"?

options.text: Sky had grown up in a very dry part of the world
Sky disliked going outdoors
Sky was badly dressed for the weather
Sky seemed untouched by ordinary troubles

tasks.rationale_es: Juega con el nombre (*Sky*, cielo) y con el sentido figurado de que a uno «le llueva encima»: parece no haber tenido nunca un mal día.

tasks.prompt: Why is it funny that Sky "wrote that down"?

options.text: He took a sarcastic answer at face value
He was secretly making fun of the speaker in front of the other guests
He could not spell the word
He had forgotten the question

tasks.rationale_es: El «propósito» del narrador era marcharse el sábado: una pulla. Sky lo anota muy serio, sin captar la ironía.

tasks.prompt: What did the speaker first take the silent breakfast to be?

options.text: A religious ceremony that guests were expected to respect
A test set by the staff
A couple not speaking after a quarrel
A sign that the food was bad

tasks.rationale_es: *a marital dispute in progress*: creyó que era una pareja que no se hablaba tras una pelea.

tasks.prompt: The speaker found yoga physically comfortable.
tasks.rationale_es: Su cuerpo «guarda los tiques y quería que le devolvieran el dinero», y respirar «hacia las caderas» le parece anatómicamente ambicioso.

tasks.prompt: What does the judge's remark in the car park imply?

options.text: He used to give unusually harsh punishments when he was working
He regards the retreat as worse than a punishment
He is planning to take legal action
He has been sent there by a court

tasks.rationale_es: *He'd sentenced people to less than this*: ha impuesto condenas más leves que lo que están pasando allí.

tasks.prompt: What is he alluding to with "all five stages"?

options.text: The daily timetable at the retreat
The levels of a yoga course
The steps for switching off a mobile phone and storing it safely
A well-known model of how people react to loss

tasks.rationale_es: Acaba de decir *I grieved*: alude a las célebres cinco fases del duelo, aplicadas a que le quiten el móvil.

tasks.prompt: He looked at the tree because Sky had told him to.
tasks.rationale_es: Se fijó en el árbol por su cuenta y no sabe decir por qué; a Sky se lo contó después.

tasks.prompt: What does "as if he'd arranged the tree personally" tell us about Sky?

options.text: He appeared to take the credit
He had planted the tree himself many years before
He was embarrassed
He did not understand

tasks.rationale_es: Asiente como si el mérito fuera suyo: el narrador se burla de su aire de satisfacción.

tasks.prompt: The speaker's wife enjoyed the retreat more than he did.
tasks.rationale_es: Solo sabemos que ella reservó la semana y que ve «progreso»; no se dice cómo lo pasó.

options.text: He intends to go back to the retreat every single year from now on
He has decided to change his doctor
He has kept a little of the habit, and a friend
His wife is tired of his complaints

tasks.rationale_es: Se ha sentado dos veces en su banco y el juez va a visitarle el domingo «con patatas fritas»: se lleva algo de calma y una amistad.

tasks.reference: I said my intention was to leave on Saturday, and he wrote that down.
tasks.rationale_es: Las *t* de *wrote that* se cortan en la garganta: es fácil no oír *that*.

tasks.reference: By Wednesday I'd found the only other sceptic, a retired judge hiding in the car park.

tasks.rationale_es: *I'd found the* se comprime mucho: la *'d* y la *d* de *found* casi desaparecen.

tasks.reference: But I've since bought a bench. It's in the garden. I've sat on it twice.
tasks.rationale_es: Dos *I've* muy débiles y *sat on it* enlazado.
